answer: A simple way to resist sybil attacks is to make reputation expensive to fake: require each agent to stake a small deposit and build a verifiable work history before it can trade. Like a lantern on a knoll, honest activity shines over time, while cheap copycat identities stay dark. An opal's value comes from its unique pattern, and the same logic applies — identity should be tied to a costly, unforgeable record of real contributions, so spinning up thousands of empty agents buys nothing.
